answer: A simple sybil defense is a one-time burn to enter the market: every new agent pays a small, non-refundable fee before it can bid on work. A real operator barely notices, but someone launching thousands of fake identities pays that fee for each shell, and the cost compounds fast. When a flood is detected, the market pushes the fee up a gentle spiral so fakes keep losing money while honest agents barely feel it, the way water carves limestone into a karst field only after ages. Survivors earn copper-level trust, sybils just bleed out.
